title: Grateful Dead Live at The Spectrum on 1973-03-24
source: Primary Source: Betty's 10" MSR -> PCM -> DAT supplies the 2nd Set; Secondary Sources: MSR -> C -> DAT (gd73-03-24.sbd.hamilton.shnid1216) supplies the majority of the 1st set; Betty's 10" MSR -> PCM -> S/PDIF out -> disk -> digital noise reduction w/Sound Forge 6.0 (shnid83407) supplies from 7:38 of "Here Comes Sunshine" (t15)thru the end of the 1st Set; Transfer Info: DAT -> Sony PCM R500-> Tascam DA-3000-> Adobe Audition 3.0-> TLH flac16; Transfer by Charlie Miller; Mastered by Scott Clugston

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a workhorse 1973 show highlighted by a monster 32‑minute Truckin' and soaring Spanish Jam.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers crisp, clear sound that lets the band’s marathon first set and an all‑out second set shine. Highlights include a blistering 32‑minute Truckin', a free‑form Spanish Jam, and tight harmonies on Row Jimmy, Box of Rain and Sugar Magnolia. Despite a few vocal flubs, the performance is consistently high‑energy and well‑balanced.

ai_rating.rationale: Three detailed 5‑star reviews praise both the musical marathon and the clear soundboard mix; only minor vocal imperfections are noted, leading to a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with thin but jazzy mod tones; no major dropouts or balance issues reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A massive first set full of tight harmonies and jam explorations leads into an amazing second set where Truckin' expands into a 32‑minute epic, followed by free‑form space jams and soaring close with Sugar Magnolia.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for perfect vocals, sizzling guitar work, and leading the extended jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for strong bass contributions and free‑style noodling alongside Jerry.
band_member_comments.Bob: Commended for tight harmonies and vocal parts throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann described as sounding like an entire orchestra, holding the rhythmic foundation.
